title: Eufy vs. Wyze vs. Blink: The Budget Security Camera Showdown Under $60 (2026)
excerpt: Three budget security camera brands that don't require monthly fees. We compare Eufy, Wyze, and Blink on video quality, free storage, reliability, and who should buy which in 2026.
author: HiddenCameras Editorial
body:
The Best Security Cameras Don't Have to Cost a Fortune

Ring and Arlo have convinced many buyers that good security cameras cost $150-300 each plus monthly subscriptions. That's simply not true in 2026. Eufy, Wyze, and Blink all offer capable cameras under $60 that store footage, send smart alerts, and work reliably — without mandatory monthly fees.

Choosing among them comes down to three things: how you want to store footage, what smart features matter to you, and which ecosystem your home is in. This comparison covers all three brands across every category that matters for day-to-day security use.

Pricing Reality Check

Eufy Indoor Cam 2K: $35-45. No hub required for basic use, 2K resolution, local microSD storage or HomeBase optional.
>Wyze v4: $35. 1080p with color night vision, free 14-day cloud storage, microSD supported. The

>Wyze v3 Pro is $45 for 2K resolution.

Blink Mini 2: $40 (2-pack $70). 1080p with color night vision, local storage via Sync Module 2 ($35 additional) or free 60-second clips in cloud, requires Amazon ecosystem.

At these prices, you can outfit a home with 4-6 cameras for what a single Ring Pro setup costs. The question is whether the budget cameras are good enough. For most home use cases, they genuinely are.

Video Quality Head-to-Head

Eufy wins on raw resolution. The 2K Indoor Cam captures noticeably more detail than 1080p competitors, and the image processing is solid across brightness ranges. Night vision on Eufy cameras is infrared black-and-white on budget models; the 2K Pan and Tilt adds color night vision via a built-in spotlight.

>Wyze v4 holds its own at 1080p with surprisingly good color night vision that activates automatically in low light. For the price, the video quality is genuinely impressive. The v3 Pro at $45 bumps to 2K and matches Eufy's image quality closely.

Blink Mini 2 delivers solid 1080p with color night vision but sits slightly behind Eufy and Wyze in image processing at night. The camera's strength is reliability and simplicity, not image perfection.

Winner: Eufy for quality, Wyze for quality-per-dollar.

Free Storage: The Critical Differentiator

This is where the brands differ most, and where buyers get surprised after purchase.

Eufy: Local storage free via microSD card (up to 256GB). Optional HomeBase adds NAS-style local storage for multiple cameras. Free cloud storage for event clips is available on select models. No subscription required for any core feature.

Wyze: 14 days of free cloud event storage with no cooldown period on the Cam v4. MicroSD supported for continuous local recording. Free cloud is the most generous of the three. Optional Cam Plus ($1.99/month) adds unlimited AI detection if needed.

Blink: Free cloud stores 60-second event clips per motion with a 60-second cooldown between clips. Local storage requires the Sync Module 2 ($35 additional, sold separately), which adds USB drive storage with no clip limits. Without the Sync Module, the free tier may not capture everything you need.

Winner: Wyze for free cloud. Eufy for true local-first storage. Blink requires additional hardware for useful storage.

Smart Detection: Person, Pet, Vehicle

Eufy: On-device AI detection for person, pet, and crying baby detection — no cloud processing, no subscription. This is Eufy's biggest technical advantage. Detection happens on the camera itself, meaning alerts are fast and private.

Wyze: Person detection is free on Cam v4 without Cam Plus. Vehicle and pet detection require Cam Plus ($1.99/month per camera). For most indoor cameras, free person detection is sufficient.

Blink: Person detection is included free. Pet and vehicle detection are not available at any price. If you need multi-category AI detection, Blink is not the right choice.

Winner: Eufy for on-device AI breadth. Wyze for free-tier AI coverage.

Reliability and App Quality

Eufy: Generally reliable with one major caveat — Eufy had a significant security incident in 2022 where some users could access other users' camera feeds. Eufy responded with end-to-end encryption improvements, but privacy-conscious buyers should research this before purchasing. The app is well-designed and feature-rich.

Wyze: Had a notable data breach in 2023 that exposed footage to unintended users for a brief period. Wyze responded quickly and implemented fixes. The app has improved significantly since 2022 and is now competitive with premium brands. Wyze's history of being honest about security incidents builds more long-term trust than brands that quietly handle them.

Blink: Strong reliability record. Being an Amazon product means robust infrastructure and consistent app updates. The Blink app is simpler than Eufy or Wyze — fewer features but fewer ways things go wrong. Deep Alexa and Amazon Echo Show integration is seamless.

Winner: Blink for reliability track record. Eufy and Wyze are both solid with noted security histories.

Ecosystem Integration

Eufy: Works with Amazon Alexa and Google Assistant. Limited HomeKit support on some models. Best within the Eufy ecosystem (multiple cameras managed through HomeBase).

Wyze: Alexa and Google Assistant. Growing Wyze ecosystem including Wyze Lock, Wyze Thermostat, and Wyze Robot Vacuum. If you're building a budget smart home, Wyze's breadth is unmatched at the price point.

Blink: Deep Amazon/Alexa integration — the best of the three for Amazon households. Works natively on Echo Show displays. Limited Google integration. Not compatible with Apple HomeKit.

Winner: Blink for Amazon households. Wyze for budget smart home builders. Eufy for Eufy multi-camera setups.

Who Should Buy Each Brand

Buy Eufy if: You want on-device AI detection with zero subscription. You prioritize local storage over cloud. You're comfortable with the brand's post-2022 security improvements. You want 2K resolution at budget pricing.

Buy Wyze if: You want the most generous free cloud storage tier. You're building a broader budget smart home (Wyze Lock, thermostat, etc.). You want good person detection for free without any subscription. The $35-45 price point with solid performance makes Wyze the best all-around value pick.

Buy Blink if: You're heavily in the Amazon/Alexa ecosystem. You want maximum simplicity and reliable infrastructure. You don't need advanced AI detection categories. You're willing to add the Sync Module 2 for proper local storage.

The Bottom Line

For most households buying their first security cameras,

>Wyze v4 ($35) with a 32GB microSD card ($8) is the strongest recommendation. Free 14-day cloud storage, solid video quality, reliable person detection, and a 3-year total cost of $43 per camera. Eufy is the pick for buyers who want on-device AI and zero cloud dependence. Blink is for Amazon households that value simplicity and deep Alexa integration over raw features.
